Alicia — great to meet you and Tom. Below is a concise post-call recap and an initial econ snapshot so your procurement and product teams have numbers to evaluate. Attaching a short spreadsheet (redwood_econ_snapshot.xlsx) with the line-item math.

Recap / assumptions we used for the worked example:
- Avg tokens per note: 600 tokens (you confirmed)
- Pilot ramp: month1 0.5M tokens -> month6 3.5M tokens
- Year1 steady state (expected): 6M tokens/month

Initial commercial options (high-level):
1) Hosted, pay-as-you-go: $1,050 per 1M tokens
   - Why: supports on-demand scale + no commit; includes streaming + 30-day logs
2) 12-month committed band: $850 per 1M tokens (committed >= 6M tokens/month)
   - Why: predictable unit cost; reserved capacity pricing

Sample math (hosted PAYG example, month6 = 3.5M tokens):
- Tokens/month: 3.5M -> cost = 3.5 * $1,050 = $3,6750 (i.e., $36,750)
- Tokens per feature (per completed note): 600 tokens -> number of notes = 3,500,000 / 600 ≈ 5,833 notes
- $ / feature (hosted PAYG) = $36,750 / 5,833 ≈ $6.30 / generated note

Unit-econ framing for CAC payback (example assumptions):
- Average paid customer ARPA contribution per clinical user per month: $75
- Assume 3 paying users/customer for the new feature on average -> incremental ARR/customer = $75 * 3 * 12 = $2,700/yr
- If incremental gross margin target on feature is 40%, allowable annual cost per customer for inference = $2,700 * (1 - 0.40) = $1,620/yr
- That implies maximum monthly inference cost per customer = $135/mo
- Break-even CAC payback target 6 months => allowed customer acquisition cost = 6 * $135 = $810

Using the hosted PAYG $/feature above ($6.30), that implies ~21 features/month per customer before inference cost hits $135/mo (21 * $6.30 ≈ $132). 

Key asks / next steps from us:
- We will run a 1-page unit-econ slide showing 2 scenarios side-by-side: PAYG vs 12mo commit, and show sensitivity to tokens per note (±20%).
- Can you confirm the three ARPA / adoption assumptions above (avg paid users per customer, target gross margin, target payback months)? If procurement gave you a hard budget band (you wrote $10k–$45k/mo), tell us if they require us to size a committed band to meet the low end.
- Proposed next touch: 30m econ review next Tue (Mar 13) — I can present the deck and run a live calculator.

Attaching redwood_econ_snapshot.xlsx (summary tab + detailed calc tab). I'll loop in Marissa for committed-band pricing and Ben for discount authorization.

Best,

Alicia — thanks again. Per our internal review we've put together two concrete options and an illustrative unit-econ worked example (attached). High level: 

Option A — Hosted PAYG (no commit)- $1,050 per 1M tokens- Pilot-friendly, fastest time-to-value

Option B — 12-month committed band (predictable unit cost)- $850 per 1M tokens (base)- With a 12M tokens/mo 12mo commit + partner credit, we can get to ~$720 per 1M tokens

Illustrative worked example (month6 ramp, hosted PAYG baseline):
- Tokens/month: 3.5M -> cost = 3.5 * $1,050 = $36,750/month
- Notes/month: 3,500,000 / 600 = 5,833 notes- $/feature = $36,750 / 5,833 ≈ $6.30/note
- If you move to committed pricing at $850/1M -> cost = 3.5 * $850 = $29,750 -> $/feature ≈ $5.10/note
- At an aggressive committed band ($720/1M) -> cost = 3.5 * $720 = $25,200 -> $/feature ≈ $4.32/note

CAC payback sensitivity (using your target 6–9 months):
- Using incremental ARPA/customer = $225/mo (3 paid users * $75 each) and a 40% gross margin target -> allowable inference spend per customer = $135/mo
- At $6.30/feature -> customer can consume ~21 notes/mo before hitting $135/mo
- If you target customers to use 60 notes/mo, inference cost = 60 * $6.30 = $378/mo -> inference would be > allowed by current ARPA assumptions; either ARPA needs to be higher OR committed pricing must be used to reduce $/feature

Margin targets and levers:
- To hit a 30–45% gross margin on the feature, we recommend one or more of: committed pricing, model quantization to reduce cost (~10–25%), prefix caching for repeat content, and a modest price-per-feature pass-through to customers. We'll model scenarios in the deck.

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm the ARPA/adoption assumptions (paid users per customer, target gross margin, payback months)?
2) If yes, I'd like to schedule Tue Mar 13 10:00 PT for a 30m econ review — I'll walk through the spreadsheet and show sensitivity ranges.
3) If procurement wants a committed band sized to $10k / month, we'll show what that looks like (e.g., 1.25M tokens = $1,312 PAYG or $1,062 committed at $850/1M pro-rate).

Attaching: redwood_econ_snapshot.xlsx (with PAYG vs committed tabs) and a draft MPA outline (healthsynapse_mpa_draft_2028-03-09.pdf) so your legal/procurement can scan. If this looks good I can send a short follow-up summary slide and invite for Tue.
